TRMM: B[i][j] += A[k][i]*B[k][j] for k>i. Dependence: B[i][j] depends on B[k][j] for k>i, so rows must be computed in decreasing i order? Actually B[i][j] reads B[k][j] for k>i, so row i must be computed after rows k>i. Original loop i increasing — wait, that reads B[k][j] which hasn't been updated yet (k>i, computed later). So original order computes with original B values for k>i? No — B[k][j] is updated when loop reaches i=k, which is after i. So B[i][j] uses pre-update B[k][j]. So dependence: iteration (i,j) reads B[k][j] written by iteration (k,j), k>i, and must read before write. So i increasing order is required (read before write). Parallelize over j: each column j independent. So parallel for over j outer, i inner sequential. Restructure:

#pragma omp parallel for private(i,k) over j, with inner i loop sequential. That's legal and good. Also could collapse? No, i has dependencies. Use schedule(static).

Write:

#pragma scop
#pragma omp parallel
#pragma omp for schedule(static) private(i,k)
  for (j...) { for (i...) { for k...; B[i][j]*=alpha; } }
#pragma endscop

j is loop var of the for. Fine.
